transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here. Those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to really scare me, and a colleague helped me realize I needed to get some help.
Have you ever had a similar period in the past when you felt this depressed or had thoughts of not wanting to wake up, or is this the first time it has happened?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time I've ever felt this way, and it’s really terrifying to be honest.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on without any clear trigger? About how long have you been feeling this way?

All of this has been weighing me down for about a month now. It really started after a stressful stretch at work with a bunch of difficult cases and a tense disagreement with my supervising clinician about treatment plans.

Since this started, have you been depressed most of the day nearly every day and lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or does it feel more like stress and worry tied mainly to the work situation? How much has this been affecting your sleep, appetite, concentration, and ability to function day to day?

It feels like a heavy, constant depression and I’ve completely lost interest in everything, even playing guitar or seeing my friends. My sleep is terrible because I lie awake ruminating, I have no appetite and am losing weight, and my brain feels so muddy that I can't concentrate. It's gotten so bad that I'm calling in sick, ignoring texts, and letting everything pile up because I just can't function.

If the work conflict were resolved or you were away from work for a few days, do you think your mood would lift noticeably, or would you still feel deeply depressed and unable to enjoy things most of the time?

Even though the work stress triggered all of this, I feel like the depression has completely taken over now. Even when I'm away from the clinic, I still feel deeply empty and can't enjoy things like playing my guitar or seeing my friends. I don't think a few days off would lift this heavy, constant cloud.

Have you had any experiences like hearing voices others can’t hear, or strongly believing things like you are guilty, ruined, or deserve punishment even when others say that isn’t true? If so, did those experiences happen only when you were feeling depressed?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never heard any voices that aren't there, and I don't hold those kinds of extreme beliefs about being ruined or deserving of punishment.
Have you had any thoughts of actually killing yourself, and if so, have you made a plan or taken any steps to prepare? Do you have access to anything you could use to hurt yourself?

Yes, I have. On my worst day, I actually drafted a suicide note on my phone and searched online for ways to kill myself, thinking it would be a relief to just not wake up. Doing that scared me so deeply, and that's why I reached out to my coworker for help.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster, or did risky things that were out of character for you? Even if it did not feel like a problem at the time, has anything like that ever happened?

No, I have never experienced anything like that at all. I've never had periods of feeling unusually energized, euphoric, or needing much less sleep in that way. It's actually been the exact opposite for me, where I just feel completely drained.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime episode of a major depressive syndrome lasting about 1 month with persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, insomnia, decreased appetite/weight loss, impaired concentration, functional decline, and suicidal ideation with preparatory behavior. No psychotic symptoms were reported, and there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes. Although work stress preceded onset, symptoms are pervasive beyond the stressor and meet criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
